title: How do you feel? Measuring User-Perceived Value for Rejecting Machine Decisions in Hate Speech Detection

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating machine learning models on both 'seen' (in-domain) and 'unseen' (out-of-domain) datasets to measure the impact of dataset bias on model confidence, error rates, and optimal human-in-the-loop rejection thresholds.

Conducting statistical analysis (Mann-Whitney U test) on survey responses to measure differences in how male and female annotators/users perceive and value hate speech classification scenarios (e.g., false positives vs. false negatives).
Using the Kruskal-Wallis test to identify statistical differences in the perception and valuation of machine-detected hate speech decisions among participants of different nationalities.
Using the Kruskal-Wallis test to measure statistical differences in hate speech perception among survey participants based on their language.
Analyzing survey data with the Kruskal-Wallis test to determine if a participant's ethnicity significantly influences their subjective perception of machine-made hate speech decisions.
Testing for statistical differences in the perceived value of hate speech moderation across participants living on different continents.
